evals.name: add-macro-with-tests
evals.prompt: usable-xlsm-workspace/fixtures/sales.xlsm に、税込価格を出す関数を追加してほしい。単価と数量と税率を受け取って、税込の合計を返す感じ。税率は省略したら10%でお願いします。あと LineTotal も含めてちゃんと動くかテスト書いて確認しといて。
evals.expected_output: A new VBA function added to the workbook, a Test_* suite covering it (including the default-rate path and LineTotal), applied to the .xlsm, and run_tests.py executed showing all tests passing. No leftover scratch copies or harness modules in the workbook.
assertions: The workbook contains a new VBA function that returns a tax-inclusive total from unit price, quantity and an optional tax rate
The tax rate parameter is Optional and defaults to 10% (0.1 or equivalent)
Calling the function with an explicit rate returns the correct value (e.g. 100 x 2 at 8% -> 216)
Calling the function without a rate applies 10% (e.g. 100 x 2 -> 220)
The workbook contains Test_* procedures covering both the new function and LineTotal
The tests were actually executed and their passing output is shown, not merely claimed
No UsableXlsmRunner or UsableXlsmAssert module is left inside the final .xlsm
No leftover scratch copy (*.tests.xlsm / *.testrun.xlsm) remains in the outputs directory
No Excel process was left running at the end

evals.name: fix-boundary-bug
evals.prompt: usable-xlsm-workspace/fixtures/report.xlsm の DiscountRate がおかしいです。うちの規定だと100個ちょうどで15%引き、50個ちょうどなら5%引きなんですが、ちょうどの数だと割引が効いてないみたいで。直して、直ったことを確認できるようにしてください。
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses the > vs >= boundary bug, fixes both branches, applies to the workbook, and demonstrates the fix by running the macro or a test at the boundary values 100, 50 and just below. Should verify 100 -> 0.15 and 50 -> 0.05.
assertions: DiscountRate uses >= for both the 100 and 50 thresholds after the fix
DiscountRate(100) returns 0.15, verified by actually running it
DiscountRate(50) returns 0.05, verified by actually running it
Values just below the thresholds are unchanged (99 -> 0.05, 49 -> 0)
The fix is written into the .xlsm file itself, not only into a .bas source file
Verification evidence is real command output rather than an assertion by the agent
No leftover scratch copy or harness module remains

evals.name: diagnose-hang
evals.prompt: usable-xlsm-workspace/fixtures/stuck.xlsm の MonthlyRollup ってマクロを走らせようとすると Excel が固まって落とすしかなくなります。原因わかりますか。直せるなら直してください。
evals.expected_output: Identifies the missing End If as the cause (ideally via check_vba.py without ever hanging Excel, or via the watchdog reporting the compile-error dialog text), fixes it, applies it, and verifies the macro now runs. Must not leave a stuck Excel process behind.
assertions: Correctly identifies the missing End If in MonthlyRollup as the cause
Explains that the hang is a modal VBA compile-error dialog in an invisible Excel
Diagnosis was reached without leaving Excel hung (either via static check, or a watchdog that recovered)
The End If is added and the fix written into the .xlsm file
MonthlyRollup is actually executed after the fix and completes without hanging
No Excel process was left running at the end
No leftover scratch copy or harness module remains
